rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly, so this candidate raises obfuscation pressure while protecting the hot floating-point kernels. spectral-norm is dominated by tiny, extremely hot FP loops (eval_A_times_u / eval_At_times_u called O(n^2) times, A[i][k] macro arithmetic), so SUB gets the highest weights since instruction substitution obscures the arithmetic identity of those inner loops with near-zero runtime penalty, and IBR is favored next to break the straight-line branch structure of the kernels. FLA and BCF receive solid SecurityGain but the highest RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights of the table, so the selector will preferentially avoid flattening/bogus-control-flow on the hottest small functions while still applying them where features tolerate it. SPLIT is kept as a cheap diversity amplifier on the larger main/eval_AtA_times_u bodies, and ICALL/IGV stay low because this program is almost call-free (a handful of leaf math functions) with essentially no global-variable surface, making those passes mostly dead weight and size overhead here.
